items.q: Which sentence can be changed into the passive voice?
items.why: 목적어(the fence)가 있는 문장만 수동태로 바꿀 수 있어요.

items.q: What is the past participle of “choose”?
items.why: choose - chose - chosen.

items.q: What is the past participle of “steal”?
items.why: steal - stole - stolen.

items.q: What is the past participle of “write”?
items.why: write - wrote - written.

items.q: What is the past participle of “drive”?
items.why: drive - drove - driven.

items.q: What is the past participle of “begin”?
items.why: begin - began - begun.

items.q: Which is the pattern for the present perfect passive?
items.why: 현재완료 수동태는 has/have been + 과거분사예요.

items.q: Which is the correct pattern for a passive sentence with “can”?
items.why: 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형 be가 오므로 can be + 과거분사예요.

items.q: Which sentence uses “by” to show who did the action?
o: She goes to school by bus.
The mural was painted by my classmates.
I will meet you by the school gate.
items.why: 나머지 by는 교통수단, 기한, 장소를 나타내요. 행위자를 나타내는 것은 수동태의 by예요.

items.q: “My bike was stolen yesterday.” 에서 수동태를 쓴 가장 알맞은 이유는?
items.why: 행위자를 모르거나 중요하지 않을 때 수동태로 대상(자전거)을 주어로 써요.

items.q: Make a yes/no question from “The photos were taken by Amy.”
o: Did the photos take by Amy?
Was the photos taken by Amy?
Were the photos taken by Amy?
Were taken the photos by Amy?
items.why: 복수 주어의 과거 수동태 의문문은 Were + 주어 + 과거분사예요.

items.q: Make a negative sentence from “The car is washed on Sundays.”
o: The car does not washed on Sundays.
The car is not washed on Sundays.
The car not is washed on Sundays.
The car is not wash on Sundays.
items.why: 수동태의 부정문은 be동사 뒤에 not을 써요.

items.q: Choose the question for this answer: “Coffee is grown in warm countries.”
items.why: 장소를 묻는 수동태 의문문은 Where + be동사 + 주어 + 과거분사예요.

items.q: Complete: “___ was the tower built? — Two hundred years ago.”
items.why: '200년 전에'라고 시간을 답했으므로 When이 알맞아요.

items.q: Complete: “She is interested ___ painting.”
items.why: be interested in은 '~에 관심이 있다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Complete: “Our town is known ___ its sweet apples.”
items.why: be known for는 '~로 유명하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Complete: “Mom is worried ___ my grades.”
items.why: be worried about은 '~에 대해 걱정하다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: How Paper Is Made
items.text: Paper is made from wood, and the process has several steps. First, trees are cut down and taken to a factory. There the wood is broken into small pieces and mixed with water. The mixture is heated until it becomes a soft, thick liquid called pulp. Next, the pulp is spread on a screen and pressed flat, and the water is removed. The thin sheets are dried and rolled into big rolls. Finally, the paper is cut to different sizes and sent to stores. Because so much paper is thrown away, many schools now collect used paper so that it can be recycled instead of wasted.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The steps used to turn wood into paper
The reasons why trees must never be cut down
The ways schools collect and sort old paper
The places where finished paper is sold
qs.why: 처음부터 끝까지 나무가 종이가 되는 과정을 순서대로 설명해요.

qs.q: What happens to the wood right after it is broken into small pieces?
o: It is rolled into big rolls.
It is cut into different sizes.
It is sent to the stores.
qs.why: 작게 부서진 뒤 물과 섞인다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “pulp” is ___.
qs.why: heated mixture becomes a soft, thick liquid called pulp.

qs.q: Why do many schools collect used paper?
o: To recycle it instead of wasting it
To burn it in the factory to make heat
To sell it back to the stores for money
To make the new paper much thinner
qs.why: so that it can be recycled instead of wasted라고 했어요.

items.title: School Festival Notice
items.text: The School Festival will be held on Saturday. The gym will be decorated by the students of Class 2-3. Posters made by the art club have already been put up in the hallways. Visitors will be welcomed at the front gate at 10 a.m., and a free lunch will be served in the cafeteria. A short play written by the drama club will be performed at 1 p.m. Please note that bicycles are not allowed inside the school yard; they must be parked outside. Students who want to help are asked to meet their teachers by 8:30 a.m.

qs.q: Why was this notice written?
o: To give information about a school event
To ask students to buy tickets for a school trip
To warn students about a sudden rule change
To thank the art club for its fine posters
qs.why: 축제 일정과 안내 사항을 알리는 글이에요.

qs.q: Who will decorate the gym?
qs.why: The gym will be decorated by the students of Class 2-3.

qs.q: What does the word “they” in the passage refer to?
qs.why: they must be parked outside는 앞의 bicycles를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Which of the following is true?
o: A play will be performed at 1 p.m.
Lunch will be served at the front gate.
Posters have not been put up yet.
Bicycles can be kept in the gym.
qs.why: 1 p.m.에 연극이 공연될 거예요.

items.title: The Story of the Bicycle
items.text: The first bicycle was made in the early 1800s. It had no pedals, so riders pushed it along the ground with their feet. Later, pedals were added to the front wheel, but these bikes were very hard to ride. The modern bicycle, with two wheels of the same size and a chain, was developed in the 1880s. It was soon loved by people of all ages because it was cheaper than a horse and easy to keep. Today, bicycles are used for sport, travel, and fun, and in many cities special lanes have been built for them.

qs.q: How did people move the first bicycle?
o: They pushed it with their feet.
They turned the pedals by hand.
They pulled it with a horse.
qs.why: It had no pedals, so riders pushed it along the ground with their feet.

qs.q: Why did people love the modern bicycle?
o: It was cheaper than a horse and easy to keep.
It had a very large front wheel and no chain.
It could carry heavy things up a hill.
It was faster than the first bicycle.
qs.why: cheaper than a horse and easy to keep라고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “developed” is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: developed는 '발전시켜 만들어졌다'는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What has been built in many cities for bicycles?
qs.why: special lanes have been built for them.

items.title: A Lost Backpack
items.text: Hi Ms. Lee, I'm writing about a bag that was lost on the school bus yesterday afternoon. It is a blue backpack with a small panda on the front. My math book, a lunch box, and a pair of glasses were left inside. I was told by the driver that lost things are kept in the office, so I went there this morning, but my bag had not been brought in yet. Could you please check again? If it is found, please call me at the number on the school list. Thank you very much. Daniel

qs.q: Why did Daniel write this email?
o: To ask for help finding his bag
To thank the bus driver kindly
To report a broken school bus
To ask about a math test
qs.why: 잃어버린 가방을 찾아 달라고 부탁하는 이메일이에요.

qs.q: Why did Daniel go to the office this morning?
o: He was told lost things are kept there.
He wanted to meet Ms. Lee in person.
He needed to borrow a new math book.
He was asked to bring his glasses.
qs.why: 기사님에게서 분실물은 사무실에 보관된다고 들었어요.

qs.q: Which thing was NOT in the bag?
qs.why: 물병은 언급되지 않았어요.

qs.q: How does Daniel probably feel?
qs.why: 가방이 없어 걱정하지만 다시 찾아봐 달라고 부탁하는 모습이에요.

items.title: From Seed to Chocolate
items.text: Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree, which is grown in warm, rainy places near the equator. After the cacao pods are picked, the seeds are taken out and left in the sun for several days. Then they are dried, cleaned, and roasted. The roasted seeds are crushed into a thick paste, and sugar and milk are added to make sweet chocolate. The finished chocolate is poured into molds and cooled before it is wrapped and sold. Many farmers depend on cacao for their income, so fair prices are important for their families.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How chocolate is made from cacao seeds
Why farmers need to move to warm places
Which shops sell the best chocolate
How sugar and milk are produced
qs.why: 카카오 씨앗이 초콜릿이 되는 과정을 설명해요.

qs.q: What is done to the seeds after they are left in the sun?
o: They are dried, cleaned, and roasted.
They are crushed into paste at once.
They are poured into molds at once.
They are wrapped and sold in stores.
qs.why: Then they are dried, cleaned, and roasted.

qs.q: Why are fair prices important?
o: Many farmers depend on cacao for money.
Chocolate is very hard to wrap well.
Cacao trees grow only in rainy weather.
Factories need less sugar and milk.
qs.why: farmers depend on cacao for their income.

qs.q: When are sugar and milk added?
o: After the seeds become a thick paste
While the seeds are left in the sun
qs.why: 씨앗을 으깨 반죽을 만든 뒤에 설탕과 우유가 더해져요.

items.title: Our Recycling Program
items.text: Our school started a recycling program last spring. Three colored boxes were placed in every classroom: blue for paper, green for plastic, and yellow for cans. At first, many students put things in the wrong boxes, so posters were hung beside them to show what goes where. Every Friday, the boxes are emptied by the cleaning staff, and the materials are picked up by a recycling truck. In six months, the amount of trash from our school was reduced by almost a third. Now our class is being asked to teach the program to students in a nearby elementary school.

qs.q: Why were posters hung beside the boxes?
o: Students often used the wrong boxes.
The boxes were too small to be seen.
The cleaning staff asked for them.
A truck could not find the boxes.
qs.why: 처음에는 많은 학생들이 잘못된 상자에 넣어서 포스터를 붙였어요.

qs.q: What color box is for cans?
qs.why: yellow for cans.

qs.q: What happened after six months?
qs.why: 쓰레기의 양이 거의 3분의 1 줄었어요.

qs.q: What can we guess about the nearby elementary school?
o: It probably has no such program yet.
It has a much bigger recycling truck.
It built the same program first.
It will close its classrooms soon.
qs.why: 이 반이 가르쳐 달라는 요청을 받은 것으로 보아 아직 같은 프로그램이 없는 것 같아요.

items.title: A Day at the Science Museum
items.text: Last Saturday, my family visited the city science museum. We were given maps at the entrance, and my little brother was thrilled by the dinosaur bones that were displayed in the main hall. The skeletons were found long ago by scientists who dug in a desert. After that, we watched a short film about stars, which was shown in a round theater. I was most impressed by a giant model of the solar system that is hung from the ceiling. We were very tired when we got home, but it was a wonderful day.

qs.q: Why did the writer write this text?
o: To tell about an enjoyable day
To explain how to build a museum
To ask readers to visit the desert
qs.why: 가족과 박물관에 다녀온 하루를 기록한 글이에요.

qs.q: How did the writer's brother feel in the main hall?
qs.why: was thrilled by the dinosaur bones라고 했어요.

qs.q: What did the family do right after seeing the dinosaur bones?
o: They watched a film about stars.
They looked at a model of the solar system.
They bought maps at the entrance.
qs.why: After that, we watched a short film about stars.

qs.q: In the passage, “impressed” means ___.
qs.why: impressed는 '깊은 인상을 받았다'는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Old Clock Tower
items.text: In the center of Maple Town stands an old clock tower. It was built in 1912 and was used as a meeting place for many years. During a big storm in 1975, the clock was badly damaged, and the tower was closed for safety. For decades, nobody paid attention to it. Then, last year, a group of students started a campaign to repair it. Money was collected at school fairs, and a skilled clockmaker was hired by the town. The repair was finished last month, and the bells can be heard across the town again. Visitors are now invited to climb the tower every Sunday.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How an old clock tower was repaired
Why a storm hit the town in 1975
Where the best school fairs are held
How a clockmaker learned his skills
qs.why: 학생들의 노력으로 낡은 시계탑이 수리된 이야기예요.

qs.q: Who started the campaign to repair the tower?
qs.why: a group of students started a campaign.

qs.q: Why was the tower closed?
o: A storm badly damaged the clock.
The money for the repair ran out.
The bells were too loud for the town.
qs.why: 큰 폭풍으로 시계가 심하게 망가졌기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does “it” refer to in “nobody paid attention to it”?
qs.why: 앞 문장의 the tower를 가리켜요.

items.title: Saving the Rainforests
items.text: Rainforests are often called the lungs of the Earth because their trees produce a large amount of oxygen. A very large number of animals and plants are found nowhere else. However, rainforests are being cut down quickly to make room for farms and roads. When a forest is destroyed, many animals lose their homes, and the soil is washed away by heavy rain. Some countries have created national parks where trees are protected by law. Everyone can help, too: by choosing paper and wood products that are labeled as responsible, we can reduce the damage.

qs.q: Why are rainforests called the lungs of the Earth?
o: Their trees produce a lot of oxygen.
They are shaped like human lungs.
They are the biggest parks in the world.
qs.why: their trees produce a large amount of oxygen.

qs.q: What happens to the soil when a forest is destroyed?
o: It is washed away by heavy rain.
It is protected by national parks.
It is carried to new roads.
qs.why: the soil is washed away by heavy rain.

qs.q: What does the writer want readers to do?
o: Move to a national park soon
Stop using all paper at home
qs.why: 책임 있게 만들어진 제품을 고르라고 제안해요.

qs.q: In the passage, “reduce” is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: reduce the damage는 '피해를 줄이다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Phones and Sleep
items.text: Smartphones are used by almost everyone today, but experts say they should be used carefully. Research shows that sleep can be disturbed by the blue light from screens. For that reason, doctors advise people to turn their phones off an hour before bed. Messages can wait until morning. Some families keep a basket near the door where all phones are placed during dinner so that conversations are not interrupted. These small habits are easy to follow, and they can make a big difference in daily life.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Small habits help us use phones wisely.
Phones should never be brought home from school.
Families should eat dinner in different rooms.
Blue light is useful for getting good sleep.
qs.why: 휴대폰을 신중하게 쓰기 위한 작은 습관들을 소개해요.

qs.q: What do doctors advise?
o: Using screens with blue light more
qs.why: turn their phones off an hour before bed.

qs.q: Why do some families use a basket during dinner?
o: So that phones can be charged faster
So that messages can be read together
So that the door stays closed
qs.why: 대화가 방해받지 않도록 하기 위해서예요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude?
qs.why: 쉽게 따를 수 있는 현실적인 조언을 해요.

items.ex: Many people want to invent something useful.
items.exko: 많은 사람들이 쓸모 있는 것을 발명하고 싶어 해요.

items.ex: Heavy rain can damage the roof of a house.
items.exko: 폭우는 집의 지붕을 손상시킬 수 있어요.

items.ex: The school will announce the winners on Friday.
